correctness.rationale: For every n>=9, the allowed connected triples in the Alexander dual are exactly four cyclic orbit types; checking one extra vertex produces exactly n consecutive four-blocks and no larger faces. Reflection-fixed simplices split into fixed vertices and swapped pairs with explicit complete counts (f,t,T,Q)=(1,(n-1)/2,2,1) in odd size, (2,(n-2)/2,4,0) for even vertex-axis, and (0,n/2,0,2) for even edge-axis. Alternating signed chain traces and the standard equivariant Alexander-duality orientation sign yield the exact stated formulas using published degree concentration. The embedded independent verifier confirms all 217 reflection cases for 9<=n<=22 on the dual and 69 direct ordinary cut-complex cases for 9<=n<=14, including all signs; finite data is not the proof for infinite n. No internal dependency on old computations.

value.rationale: An infinite natural family already has complete nonequivariant and cyclic-restricted classifications, but these leave the dihedral representation undetermined. The new formulas complete the missing reflection part and quantitatively separate the two geometrically distinct reflection conjugacy classes at even lengths: (0,2) for length ten and (1,-3) for length twelve. The structural fixed-face orbit argument explains the parity dependence and supplies information useful for equivariant and quotient topology, beyond Betti numbers or known tables.
